title: The underlying sheaf of sets of a directed colimit of sheaves of modules is the colimit of the underlying sheaves of sets
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of rings on $X$ and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I$ be a directed set and $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ a system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$ with a colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_i)_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal F$, with the maps of sheaves of sets underlying the $c_i$, is a colimit of the system of underlying sheaves of sets of the $\mathcal F_i$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (lemma-limits-colimits, line 204), part (2): colimits in Mod(O_X) are the sheafification of the presheaf colimit; with Sheaves, Lemma 007O (lemma-properties-algebraic-structures, item (7): a filtered colimit of modules has as underlying set the colimit of the underlying sets), Sheaves, Lemma 0087 (lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures (1): the underlying sheaf of sets of the sheafification of a presheaf of algebraic structures is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of sets) and Section 009E (section-limits-sheaves, item (3)). Stacks uses this silently when applying Sheaves 009F (sheaves of sets) to O_X-modules in the proof of Modules 01BS.

proof.text: Form the presheaf $\mathcal P$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules by the sectionwise colimit $\mathcal P(U)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)$. The sheafification of $\mathcal P$ is a colimit of the $\mathcal F_i$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, so it is canonically isomorphic to the given colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_i))$; this is the colimit construction in Modules 01AH(2), also recorded for arbitrary diagrams by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. For each open $U$, the filtered-colimit module lemma [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] identifies the underlying set of $\mathcal P(U)$ with the colimit of the sets $\mathcal F_i(U)$, compatibly with restrictions. Thus the underlying presheaf of sets of $\mathcal P$ is the objectwise colimit of the underlying presheaves of sets of the $\mathcal F_i$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (lemma-limits-colimits), part (2), together with Sheaves, Lemma 007O (lemma-properties-algebraic-structures), item (7), and Section 009D (section-limits-presheaves)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying sheaf of sets of the module sheafification of $\mathcal P$ is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of sets of $\mathcal P$. Transporting along the canonical isomorphism between this module sheafification and $\mathcal F$ identifies the underlying maps with the maps induced by the $c_i$.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), with Sheaves, Lemma 0087 (lemma-sheafify-presheaf-structures), item (1)

proof.text: The sheafification of the objectwise presheaf colimit is a colimit in sheaves of sets by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-colimit-sheafification]. Applying this to the underlying presheaves from Step 1 and the identification in Step 2 proves that the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal F$, with the underlying maps of the $c_i$, is the colimit of the underlying sheaves of sets of the $\mathcal F_i$.
